phrase: Let's assign clear action items before we wrap up.
useCase: Ensuring that specific tasks are delegated before the meeting ends
example: We've had a productive discussion. Let's assign clear action items before we wrap up so everyone knows what they're responsible for.
practicePrompt: The meeting is winding down but no tasks have been assigned. Ensure action items are set using this phrase.

phrase: Who will take ownership of this task?
useCase: Asking the group to identify the person responsible for a specific task
example: We need someone to prepare the client presentation. Who will take ownership of this task?
practicePrompt: A task has been discussed but no one has volunteered. Ask for an owner using this phrase.

phrase: Can you have this completed by end of week?
useCase: Setting a specific deadline for a deliverable
example: The revised budget needs to go to finance by Monday. Can you have this completed by end of week?
practicePrompt: You're assigning a task to a colleague. Set a clear deadline using this phrase.

phrase: I'll take the lead on this and report back by...
useCase: Volunteering to own a task and committing to a specific follow-up date
example: I'll take the lead on this and report back by next Wednesday with a detailed proposal.
practicePrompt: A task needs an owner and you're willing to take it on. Volunteer using this phrase.

phrase: Let's document the action items and share them with the team.
useCase: Ensuring that all assigned tasks are recorded and distributed to relevant participants
example: We've covered a lot of ground today. Let's document the action items and share them with the team so nothing falls through the cracks.
practicePrompt: The meeting produced several assignments. Ensure they're documented and shared using this phrase.

phrase: What are the next steps and who is responsible for each?
useCase: Requesting a clear breakdown of follow-up tasks and their owners
example: Before we close, what are the next steps and who is responsible for each? I want to make sure we leave with full clarity.
practicePrompt: A meeting is ending but the path forward is unclear. Ask for a clear breakdown using this phrase.

phrase: I'll follow up with an email summarizing the action items.
useCase: Committing to send a written summary of tasks assigned during the meeting
example: Great session, everyone. I'll follow up with an email summarizing the action items, owners, and deadlines by end of day.
practicePrompt: You've been taking notes during the meeting. Offer to send a summary email using this phrase.

phrase: Let's set a deadline for each action item.
useCase: Ensuring every task has a specific due date rather than being left open-ended
example: We have four tasks to complete before the launch. Let's set a deadline for each action item so we can track progress effectively.
practicePrompt: Tasks have been assigned but without due dates. Ensure deadlines are set using this phrase.

phrase: Can we prioritize these action items in order of urgency?
useCase: Ranking tasks by urgency to help the team focus on the most critical items first
example: We have a long list of follow-ups. Can we prioritize these action items in order of urgency so we tackle the most time-sensitive ones first?
practicePrompt: The team has many tasks but limited capacity. Suggest prioritizing by urgency using this phrase.

phrase: I'll check in on the progress of these items at our next meeting.
useCase: Committing to review the status of assigned tasks at the next recurring meeting
example: I'll check in on the progress of these items at our next meeting. Please reach out before then if you run into any blockers.
practicePrompt: You want to ensure tasks don't get forgotten. Commit to checking progress using this phrase.
